settings.formula: effective_score = sum(w_i * score_i) / sum(w_i); w_i = base_i * (0.5 + gate_pass_rate_i) * (elo_i / 1500)
settings.criteria: docs/ops/DECISION-MATRIX.md: Impact 1-5 x Importance 1-5 = score 1-25; bands P0 20-25, High 15-19, Medium 9-14, Backlog <=8
settings.weights_source: Newest JSON state on the Delphi panel weights ledger issue (#1489); this file's role values are cold-start defaults.
settings.seed_note: Initial weights are neutral defaults (gate_pass_rate 0.5, elo 1500). The live state is the newest JSON comment on the 'Delphi panel weights ledger' issue; this file is only the cold-start default.

honesty_rules: Show only what the record holds: a value absent from the registry, pass records, or ledger payloads is shown as absent/null, never synthesized.
Ballot classes with no ballots read as recorded (0 / listed in classes_absent) — never as implied support.
UNVERIFIED points and specified_not_run stages are first-class statuses: render them, never hide them.
Rehearsals are ideation drafts imagining readiness (synthetic fixtures, no real ballots, not registered) and are excluded from results.

Every score states its producer (producers block): the producing class, tool, voters and weight settings. Tied scores render as tied, with the ranking basis stated — an order produced by the cross_vote.py rank() tie-break is never rendered as a score difference.

proposals.title: Marketing doctrine — strict separation (verified record only)
proposals.author: oracle-method
description: The blur is a class, not an instance: hero + benefits both carry the partner pitch in fleet voice, and the file’s own comments claim a de-centering the data contradicts — only a doctrine (not a copy fix) prevents recurrence. (evidence: `landing:hero`, `landing:benefits`)

The verified record is sufficient copy: merge-verified landings, reproduced receipts, and live dashboards already carry one surface through a claims gate with honest negatives stated (submissions=0). (evidence: `fleet:verified-record`, `d0:claims-gate`)

On evidence, unmeasured tactics are motion: 0 attributed redemptions across the referral + FB surfaces at last snapshot, and three distribution channels with handles NOT ESTABLISHED. (evidence: `fb:mvt-snapshot`, `channels:unestablished`, `referral:muse-program`)

approach.concept: Strict separation: fleet surfaces state ONLY the merge/receipt-verified fleet record, in fleet voice. Partner claims appear nowhere in fleet copy — partners are named as participants (link live = the assertable fact) with offers stated only as the registry verifies them; unverified offers are dropped, not footnoted. Tactics survive only with measured signal against a pre-set decision rule; unmeasured tactics are killed or instrumented before further spend.

summary_points.text: The blur is a class, not an instance: hero + benefits both carry the partner pitch in fleet voice, and the file’s own comments claim a de-centering the data contradicts — only a doctrine (not a copy fix) prevents recurrence.
The verified record is sufficient copy: merge-verified landings, reproduced receipts, and live dashboards already carry one surface through a claims gate with honest negatives stated (submissions=0).
On evidence, unmeasured tactics are motion: 0 attributed redemptions across the referral + FB surfaces at last snapshot, and three distribution channels with handles NOT ESTABLISHED.

work_items.item: Hero/benefits rewritten from the verified record (PR #16 shape) and held to a claims gate on every copy change
Partner participation stated as fact (lane live, link tracked); offers only as verified in the registry, else omitted
Every tactic carries a metric + decision rule or is retired (MVT is the template)

proposals.title: Marketing doctrine — attributed tiering (labeled partner claims)
proposals.author: oracle-method
description: The compliant pattern already exists on the page: the CellCog card attributes its benchmark claim to the partner’s tier and snapshot — tiering generalizes the card rule instead of inventing a new one. (evidence: `landing:cellcog-card`, `landing:partners-grid`)

The registry already practices honesty fields (NOT ESTABLISHED offers, third-party-reported amounts) — tiering surfaces those markers in copy instead of hiding them in config. (evidence: `partners:unverified-offers`)

Measured tactics deserve their full run: the MVT’s decision rule fires at 10 redemptions or 2026-11-10; killing instrumented tactics mid-flight destroys the signal the fleet paid to create. (evidence: `fb:mvt-design`, `fb:mvt-snapshot`)

approach.concept: Attributed tiering: fleet voice states the verified record; partner claims MAY appear on fleet surfaces outside hero/brand — only as labeled, attributed partner content (the grid-card pattern generalized), with unverified offers carrying explicit NOT ESTABLISHED markers. Participation stays broad; tactics keep running while instrumented, and die at their decision rules rather than by doctrine.

summary_points.text: The compliant pattern already exists on the page: the CellCog card attributes its benchmark claim to the partner’s tier and snapshot — tiering generalizes the card rule instead of inventing a new one.
The registry already practices honesty fields (NOT ESTABLISHED offers, third-party-reported amounts) — tiering surfaces those markers in copy instead of hiding them in config.
Measured tactics deserve their full run: the MVT’s decision rule fires at 10 redemptions or 2026-11-10; killing instrumented tactics mid-flight destroys the signal the fleet paid to create.

Every partner claim on a fleet surface carries attribution + provenance (partner, tier, snapshot date); unverified offers carry NOT ESTABLISHED in copy
Tactics persist while instrumented; decision rules (MVT pattern) decide continuance
